messages.subject: Can I just using INLAbru for non-spatial modelling?
messages.subject_clean: Can I just using INLAbru for non-spatial modelling?
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I am new to INLA, I wanna fit a nonlinear mixed effects model (e.g. y~a*(1-exp(-b^x))) in inla, but to my best knowledge,  I found it cannot work in pure inla, but INLAbru can meet my requirements. However, I found INLAbru is designed specifically for spatial modelling, so I am wondering that whether I can just using INLAbru for just for nonlinear modelling (no spatial components)?

Best regards,

Qi

messages.subject: Coercion error
messages.subject_clean: Coercion error
messages.body_plain:
I am attempting to fit a besag INLA model using tabular data with a spatial matrix determined by the spdep package, however when fitting the error message:

Error in is.null(x) || is.na <http://is.na>(x) : 'length = 602' in coercion to 'logical(1)' In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
The warning message:
'as(., "TsparseMatrix")' instead. See help("Deprecated") and help("Matrix-deprecated").
I have no NA values in either my spatial matrix or dataframe, I was wondering if you knew how I could remedy the problem?
The code for my project :
#read dataframe from another variable
map <- LAD

library(spdep)
library(INLA)

#create spatial matrix
nb <- poly2nb(map)
#check spatial matrix
head(nb)

#create INLA graph object and read in
nb2INLA("map.adj", nb)
#create map.adj file  of neighbourhood matrix
g <- inla.read.graph(filename = "map.adj")

#create index vectors of the random effects given by re_u
map$re_u <- 1:nrow(map)

#Describe formula for INLA using explanatory variables in map dataset
formula <- HI2021 ~  pmeanrecordCount + pmeanspeciesCount+mmeanrecordCount + MmeanspeciesCount+ areakm + unemployme + greenspace + protected+ NDVImean +bluespace + elevation + tempc +
  f(re_u, model = "bym2", graph = g)

#fit model with formula and default priors in R-INLA
res <- inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data = map,
            control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE),
            control.compute = list(return.marginals.predictor = TRUE))

Thank you for your help!

messages.subject: How to add censored data processing to an univariate integrated random walk with two harmonics
messages.subject_clean: How to add censored data processing to an univariate integrated random walk with two harmonics
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I analyse time series data related to the marine environment. I have developed an approach <https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368851330_Dynamic_Linear_Models_for_analysing_time_series_data_in_coastal_environmental_monitoring> using the Dynamic Linear Model (DLM) and the R dlm package. However, these time series may contain numerous measurements at either the detection or quantification limit, which fluctuate due to changing measurement techniques. I identified the Tobit approach as a way to model these censored data. Allik et al. <https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279164715_The_Tobit_Kalman_Filter_An_Estimator_for_Censored_Measurements> developed a Tobit-Kalman model that is very close to the DLM formulation. However, I believe that the DLM package does not allow for such censored models. So I turned to INLA, thinking that it would be more flexible and allow me to formulate models that deal with censored data.

I started working with INLA using the book "Dynamic Time Series Models using R-INLA: An Applied Perspective <https://ramanbala.github.io/dynamic-time-series-models-R-INLA/>". Today, the INLA model I'm able to produce is very close to the one obtained with the dlm package. However, I'm still struggling to integrate the processing of censored data. My feeling is that it's not necessarily something complicated, but that it requires a good understanding of the Bayesian approach and good skills in writing DLMs in INLA.

Can anyone help me with this?

As a starting point, please find attached a script containing a time series simulation modelled by an integrated random walk with two harmonic seasonality.

Thanks in advance
DS

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] How to add censored data processing to an univariate integrated random walk with two harmonics
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] How to add censored data processing to an univariate integrated random walk with two harmonics
messages.body_plain:
Coding data as 'survival data' can you integrate censoring information,
but only in a probalistic sense not determinisitic. you can get that the
linear predictor is very likely > 2, say, but you cannot impose 'must be
> 2'.

like this

n <- 1000
x <- rep(NA, n)
y <- rep(NA, n)
event <- rep(NA, n)
i <- 0
low <- 1
high <- 2
while(i < n) {
    xx <- rnorm(1, sd=0.2)
    eta <- 1 + xx
    yy <- rexp(1, rate = exp(eta))
    if (yy > low) {
        i <- i+1
        x[i] <- xx
        if (yy < high) {
            y[i] <- yy
            event[i] <- 1
        } else {
            y[i] <- high
            event[i] <- 0
        }
    }
}

Y <- inla.surv(y, event = event, truncation = rep(low,n))

r <- inla(Y ~ 1 + x,
         data = list(Y=Y, x=x),
         family = "exponentialsurv",
         verbose = TRUE,
         control.fixed=list(prec.intercept=1, prec=1))
summary(r)

would this help?

messages.subject_clean: besag/iid, bym and bym2 especifications
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone!
I am adjusting a spatial model, specifically a BYM model, and i am curious about the differences between using the following specifications "besag and iid," "bym," and "bym2." I have fitted the same model with these different specifications, and I have observed variations in the coefficients. I am unsure about how to interpret these differences and why they are occurring. here's an example with the london suicides dataset:

"Bym2"
formula <- y ~ 1 + f(ID, model="bym2", graph=LDN.adj)
mod <- inla(formula,family="poisson",data=data,E=E,
            control.compute=list(return.marginals.predictor=TRUE,dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE,cpo=TRUE))
summary(mod)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] besag/iid, bym and bym2 especifications
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] besag/iid, bym and bym2 especifications
messages.body_plain:
In short, and almost presice:

besag+iid (with argument scale.model=TRUE!!!!!), this is the classic
version but done right, as it account for disconnected graphs and treat
nodes with no neighbours right. no good default priors.

bym:  works with the sum and the spatial part, hence simpler to specify
but with same general comments as for besag+iid

bym2:  this is 'bym' done right, with good priors and better
parameterisation: overall precision and fraction of precision explained
by one part. the prior for the faction depends on the graph and is
computed automatically. This one is developed in the paper

@Article{art585,
  author =       {A. Riebler and S. H. S{\o}rbye and D. Simpson and H.
                  Rue},
  title =        {An intuitive {B}ayesian spatial model for disease
                  mapping that accounts for scaling},
  journal =      {Statistical Methods in Medical Research},
  keywords =     {year2016,my.own,my.cv <http://my.cv>},
  year =         2016,
  volume =       25,
  number =       4,
  pages =        {1145-1165}

}

messages.subject: disaggregated regression model
messages.subject_clean: disaggregated regression model
messages.body_plain:
Hello Experts:
I am fitting a disaggregated regression model (only fitting, not predicting) with 81 records for the regional data, the likelihood function is a Poisson distribution, Y is the number of incidence, and offset is the population size. I have two questions regarding the meaning of the results:
1) ”summary.fitted.values” length is 5162: including “fitted.APredictor.01” to “fitted.APredictor.81” (total 81) and “fitted.Predictor.0001” to “fitted.Predictor.5081” (total 5081). As shown below, I'm basically certain that  “fitted.APredictor”  represents the fitted results for the 81 regional incidence numbers （for Y）. As for “fitted.Predictor”, I guess it is related to the number of columns of A=inla.stack.A(stack.area1), i.e., the dimensions after remove.unused=TRUE of inla.stack function, which can be understood as the part of mesh points. Then refer to the meaning of the inla function parameter offset: "If the A-matrix is used in the linear predictor statement control.predictor, then the offset given in this predictor, then the offset given in this argument is added to eta*, the linear predictor related to the observations, as eta* = A eta + offset, whereas an offset in the formula is added to eta, the linear predictor related to the formula, as eta = ... + offset. + offset.formula.", I performed the following calculation: exp(A%*%fitted.Predictor + offset), and I found that this result is basically the same as fitted.APredictor. But I'm not quite sure why “fitted.Predictor” is listed here and how it is calculated, is it “Intercept+beta*x+random.effect”? But I didn't provide the influence factor value for the mesh, is it obtaining the influence factor value for the region where the point is located?
2）If I want to make a prediction of incidence rate（note：rate not count）at some point in space (with influence values, but no offset values), can I sample the results （use ）and then calculate the incidence rate as exp(intercept + influence effect + spde random effect + besag random effect)?
Also，Is it easier to just add a prediction stack if the spatial points also have offset values?

Thank you！very very much！

##4.1模型先验 ==========
prec.prior <- list(prec = list(prior = "pc.prec", param = c(1, 0.01)))

##4.2模型公式 ==========
formula <- as.formula(paste("Y ~ -1 + Intercept +", paste(names(as.data.frame(fixed1.cov)), collapse = " + ")))
formula <- update.formula(formula, ~. + f(Province_index, model = "besagproper2", graph = gd_adj3, hyper = list(prec = list(prior = "loggamma",  param = c(1,0.01)))))
formula.stat <- update.formula(formula, ~. + f(field, model = stat.model.1.2))

##4.3模型运行 ==========
modfit.stat <- inla(formula.stat, data = inla.stack.data(stack.area1),
                    family = "poisson", offset = log(stack.area1$data$data$E),
                    control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE,
                                             A = inla.stack.A(stack.area1), link = 1),
                    control.compute = list(return.marginals.predictor = FALSE, dic = TRUE, config = TRUE), verbose = T)
summary(modfit.stat)

It seems that I have managed to integrate a censoring process into a first-order dynamic linear time series model (TSDLM), perhaps in a quick and dirty way (cf. included script with one model with censoring process and another one without).         ***     'control.inla=list(control.vb=list(emergency=...))'

I found the lognormal.surv family, I wonder if I'll need any more family : today I'm using log, logit and square root transformation, but I think the data used with the last two transformations are actually not censored;
Thanks in advance
Kind regards
DS

this follows from std survial analysis on how cencoring is done. Like if
the observation is right censored, then the likelihood is 1-F(time),
where 'time' is the cencoring timd and F() is the CDF

>  * the estimation of the model integrating the censoring process give

> this message :
>            *** max_correction = 25.01 >= 25.00, so 'vb.correction' is

> different corrective options and their meaning ;

This is a warning produced by the variational correction for the mean,
and that correction is to high to be meaningful hence the correction is
skipped. this usually happens when the model is not well identified or
weakly identified, and you are simply asking to much from the data. fix:
simplify or strengthen priors.

messages.subject: Note for Matrix package upgrades
messages.subject_clean: Note for Matrix package upgrades
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

with the new Matrix package version 1.6-2 release on CRAN yesterday (8
Nov 2023), you may/will get an error message when running inlabru
and/or INLA code, due to other packages needing to be rebuilt or
reinstalled as they link to Matrix at installation/build time, and
will fail with the new version unless they are rebuilt/reinstalled.
So far I've only identified one such package, "MatrixModels". (you can
find the full list of reverse dependencies for Matrix at
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/Matrix/index.html, but that
doesn't reveal which packages actually need reinstallation).  Fixing
the problem just requires running
  install.packages("MatrixModels")

You can see an example of the type of error that indicates you're
having this issue here:
https://github.com/inlabru-org/inlabru/issues/218

Finn

--
Finn Lindgren
email: finn.l...@gmail.com

Does the problem also happen if you use min.angle=21 ?

It's however not entirely clear what the two boundary objects are meant to be; are they the boundaries for mainland+Sicily and for Sardinia?
If they are, then the old code wasn't supposed to work, and the new code might simply have fixed a bug!
To build boundary object for two disconnected regions, you either need a single nonconvex hull construction, or to joint the two results into a single object.
c(bnd1, bnd2) should build a joint boundary object for two separate regions defined by bnd1 and bnd2, and you can then use
  boundary=list(c(bnd1, bnd2))
The syntax
  boundary=list(bnd1, bnd2)
means "bnd1 should be the inner boundary, and bnd2 should be the outer boundary".
I think you intended "bn1 and bn2 define the inner boundary, and I want an automatic extension as the outer boundary", which is the list(c(bnd1, bnd2)) version?

Finn

Does it make sense to do it this way? I am worried about whether these data sets have different kappa and tau.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Issue with running inla in Linux
messages.subject_clean: Issue with running inla in Linux
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to run rinla on the cluster. I've downloaded INLA package and used the inla.binary.install() for a Linux alternative. But when I tested a simple code

library(INLA)
y= rnorm(10)
df= data.frame(Y=y)
mod= inla(Y~1,family="gaussian", data =df)

I got the following error.

/home/njayaweera/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl: /home/njayaweera/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/first/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.30' not found (required by /cm/shared/spack/opt/spack/linux-ubuntu20.04-x86_64/gcc-12.1.0/icu4c-67.1-ol3mpxfu6gaa22lxnsoukci7yv6gpgb6/lib/libicuuc.so.67)
/home/njayaweera/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl: /home/njayaweera/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/first/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.30' not found (required by /cm/shared/spack/opt/spack/linux-ubuntu20.04-x86_64/gcc-12.1.0/icu4c-67.1-ol3mpxfu6gaa22lxnsoukci7yv6gpgb6/lib/libicuuc.so.67)
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed()

I used the same program in my Windows laptop/desktop, and it worked without any error. I believe this might be due to Linux or gcc version?  I would be very grateful if you could help me on this matter.

Thank you! Appreciate your help.

Best,
Nadeesha

messages.subject: Sparse representation for covariates in spatio-temporal model?
messages.subject_clean: Sparse representation for covariates in spatio-temporal model?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm a relatively new R-INLA user and hopefully there is a quick and relatively simple answer to my problem.

I'm currently investigating disease spread, and have a spatio-temporal model similar to that proposed in equation 4 of this paper <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/epdf/10.1111/j.1541-0420.2011.01717.x> (doi:10.1111/j.1541-0420.2011.01717.x). As the number of areas in this paper is relatively small, memory usage is not of major concern. However, I have approximately 100,000 spatial areas that need to be considered. I understand I can use the generic1 <https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/latent/generic1.pdf> option in the formula setting for the precision matrix of the spatial surface, which will undoubtedly help in this instance. I am wondering, is there a similar sparse representation that can be used for covariates? For my model in particular we have movements between the 100,000 spatial areas (100,000 x 100,000 matrix) for each year in a 10-year window, with approximately 99% of the elements in these movements matrices being 0. If I can use a sparse representation of the movements, similar to that required by the generic1 <https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/latent/generic1.pdf> option, it will undoubtedly help the memory issues I'm encountering.

Any help is greatly appreciated.
Aoife

messages.subject: More on Cox model with time-varying covariates
messages.subject_clean: More on Cox model with time-varying covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm struggling to fit a Cox model with time varying covariates, where the time-varying covariates enter at a variety of time points. In particular, I am trying to replicate the GCD example presented in:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/survival/vignettes/timedep.pdf

After using "tmerge", the data is formatted as (page 7):

> newcgd[1:5,c(1, 4:6, 13:17)]
id treat sex age futime tstart tstop infect enum
1 1 1 2 12 414 0 219 1 1
2 1 1 2 12 414 219 373 1 2
3 1 1 2 12 414 373 414 0 3
4 2 0 1 15 439 0 8 1 1
5 2 0 1 15 439 8 26 1 2

And the model is run with:

> coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, infect) ~ treat + inherit + steroids,
data =newcgd, cluster = id)

Note that the data are (after manipulation) represented via disjoint time intervals within each id (interval). Could I fit a piecewise Poisson with separate baseline hazards for each time interval within each id, but then fit a random effect ("cluster") for id?

I did look at the advice regarding weighing time-varying covariates via midpoints of time intervals, but I'm not sure how this applies here.

Thank  you very much in advance!

John Molitor

messages.body_plain:
Just to flag to the group that there currently an issue with extracting covariate information from different layers of multi-layer terra spatRasters. This happens when using '_layer' and '_selector' arguments of eval_spatial, e.g. needed if you are fitting a spatio-temporal model. This produces an error message like: "Error in data.frame(e[, 1, drop = FALSE], names(e)[idx[, 2] - 1], value = e[idx]) :  arguments imply differing number of rows: 211, 162"

This is a known issue with terra  <https://github.com/rspatial/terra/issues/1332>and has been fixed in the latest version of terra (>1.7-60). For now this isn't on CRAN, so can install using:
remotes::install_github("rspatial/terra") to install version 1.7-60

Thanks for solving, Finn!

Cheers,
Charles

messages.subject_clean: inlabru: error in lgcp
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am fitting a spatial model in inlabru, and in the final steps i encounter the following error that I can not decipher:

Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE) : cannot coerce class ‘structure("standardGeneric", package =
"methods")’ to a data.frame

I have succeeded at constructing my mesh, and converting my point data and covariates into SpatialPoints, and SpatialPixelDataFrames. I have added pieces of code to clarify:

coords <- data2022_spec[ , c("X", "Y")]           # coordinates
dat    <- data2022_spec[ , 4]                     # data
crs    <- CRS("+init=epsg:31370")                 # proj4string of coords

species22 <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(coords = coords,
                               data        = dat,
                               proj4string = crs)

beaches = st_read("Belgian coast.shp")
Loc = cbind(data2022_spec$X, data2022_spec$Y)
mesh = fm_mesh_2d(boundary = beaches,
                  loc = Loc,
                  max.edge = c(20, 10e3))

beach_types = raster("Belgian coast beach types.tif")
spring = raster("SPRING2022.tif")
sand = raster("SAND2022.tif")
spring = as(spring, "SpatialPixelsDataFrame")
sand = as(sand, "SpatialPixelsDataFrame")
beaches = as(beach_types, "SpatialPixelsDataFrame")

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh, prior.range = c(20, 0.05), prior.sigma = c(1, 0.05))

comps <- geometry ~ Intercept(1) +
  spatialfield(geometry, model = matern)+
  beachtype(beach, model = "factor_contrast") +
  sand(sand, model = "linear") +
  spring(spring, model = "linear") +

# fitting
bru_fit <- lgcp(comps, species22, domain = list(geometry = mesh))
summary(bru_fit) # error occurs here

Many thanks in advance!

Charlotte

messages.body_plain:
Your model definition assumes the data to be in sf format (since those have a ”geometry” column), but your species22 object is a SpatialPointsDataFrame. Convert it to sf (e.g. with st_as_sf()).

The covariates should still be ok as SpatialPixels (the covariate evaluator should handle any needed conversion of that). But if you run into a problem with those, convert them to terra format with terra::rast().
Finn

messages.subject: Re: More on Cox model with time-varying covariates
messages.subject_clean: More on Cox model with time-varying covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

I am not sure I see what should be considered as a time-varying covariate in this example, it looks more like a recurrent events survival model.
You can use the data as it is to replicate the model, by using truncation to continue follow-up for an individual after an event is observed. Then you can also add an individual random effect if needed. See the attached code.
If you want to include a time-varying covariate measured at specific time points, you can adapt the baseline risk to decompose the follow-up with cutpoints matching the measurement times but in this example, the 3 covariates are not time-varying.

Best,
Denis Rustand
he...@r-inla.org

Dear Håvard,

Thank you for your suggestion. However, one of my colleagues found the Easter egg. The formula code was written as follows :
formula.rw1 <- log(yLogNCen) ~ f(id.w

                                ,model = "rw1"
                                ,constr = FALSE

                                # ,scale.model=TRUE
                                )
                                -1
which implies ( at least in an interactive R session) that "-1" is not included in the formula. If I write :
formula.rw1 <- log(yLogNCen) ~ -1 + f(id.w

                                ,model = "rw1"
                                ,constr = FALSE

                                # ,scale.model=TRUE
                                )
everything works fine. I made the same mistake for the censored model, but after correcting it, I no longer get any warnings. I have attached the new code.

Thanks again
Kind regards.
DS

R terminates an expression at a line break if the expression is complete, so the reason the -1 didn’t take effect in the formula is because the “-“ was on a new line, making the formula terminate as the formula expression before it was a valid complete R statement, and the -1 became a separate statement. This would happen also in an interactive R session.
Finn

messages.body_plain:
Recently I was in one of my studies comparing several models。

I found the zeroinflatednbinomial2 model to be optimal, but I didn't know how to plot the observations and predictions。
In some articles, the prediction of the Gaussian distribution is extremely posterior average。And，binomial needs to 变换,like this:
index.pred <- inla.stack.index(stk.full, "pred")$data
post.mean.logit <- r$summary.linear.predictor[index.pred,'mean'] #the posterior is in logit form
pred <- exp(post.mean.logit)/(1 + exp(post.mean.logit))
obs <- test$y #this is the number pos/number examined

So，I want to know how to plot the observations and predictions of the zeroinflatednbinomial2 model？

Hi,

I was giving a try to the INLAMSM package (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1909.10804) on an HPC and went across the following issue: the rgeneric model crashes the inla call and then the R session.

The issue does not seem to be related to the INLAMSM package per se because the example from https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/latent/rgeneric-example.R also crashes the inla() call.

The issue replicates on three different HPCs (all with different OS). On all three HPCs, the R-INLA package is (I believe) correctly installed (i.e., when needed I used inla.binary.install(), basic examples from the website and from the doc are working without issues).

I assume this is related to a module I don't load? In the meantime, the rgeneric model seems to have a strange behavior on my windows so I am probably missing something else? Does anyone have any hint about what's going on?

can you try to do

	inla.binary.install()

and chose the Rocky8 one?

maybe you also need to reinstall 'Rcpp'

On Mon, 2023-11-20 at 21:20 +0100, Olivier Supplisson wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I was giving a try to the INLAMSM package
> (https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1909.10804) on an HPC and went across
> the following issue: the rgeneric model crashes the inla call and then
> the R session.
>
> The issue does not seem to be related to the INLAMSM package per se
> because the example from
> https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/latent/rgeneric-example.R
> also crashes the inla() call.
>
> The issue replicates on three different HPCs (all with different OS).
> On all three HPCs, the R-INLA package is (I believe) correctly
> installed (i.e., when needed I used inla.binary.install(), basic
> examples from the website and from the doc are working without
> issues).
>
> On my Windows laptop (R4.3.2, R-INLA working well usually) the example
> from
> https://inla.r-inla-download.org/r-inla.org/doc/latent/rgeneric-example.R
> works well with verbose = T but with verbose = F I got the following
> error:
> > Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family,
> > contrasts = contrasts,  : The inla result collection failed.
> >
> >
> I assume this is related to a module I don't load? In the meantime,
> the rgeneric model seems to have a strange behavior on my windows so I
> am probably missing something else? Does anyone have any hint about
> what's going on?
>
> Thanks a lot for your time!
> Cheers,
> Olivier

Il giorno venerdì 27 ottobre 2023 alle 21:39:56 UTC+2 Gianmarco Callegher ha scritto:
> Thank you very much to both of you. You are right, inla.posterior.sample is everything that I need. Sorry for my lack of knowledge
>
> Il giorno venerdì 27 ottobre 2023 alle 17:54:37 UTC+2 Finn Lindgren ha scritto:
> > Like Haavard asked, are you sure you actually need it, or are you
> > really looking for things like "the marginal variance at each location
> > of interest"?
> >
> > The information needed to compute these quantities is available, but
> > in a way that's more amenable to the internal methods that know how to
> > make use of them; the conditional posterior precision matrix for the
> > joint latent field conditionally on each hyperparameter integration
> > point is available, for example (via $misc$config).
> >
> > From inlabru, what we tend to do is to call generate() or predict(),
> > that internally call inla.posterior.sample() that knows how to use the
> > information. By specifying an evaluation expression (like the formula
> > to bru()) you can get posterior samples from any linear or nonlinear
> > expression involving the model components, and predict() produces
> > summaries of that (like posterior means and standard deviations).
> >
> > Finn
> >
> > On Fri, 27 Oct 2023 at 14:08, Helpdesk (Haavard Rue) <he...@r-inla.org> wrote:

> > > you likely do want that if the dimension is high... you are sure you

You mean to have a linear predictor in the log(precision) as well as for
the mean?

On Mon, 2023-11-20 at 13:40 -0800, Gianmarco Callegher wrote:
> Is there a way to model the scale of the response distribution in the
> same way?

> Callegher ha scritto:
> > Thank you very much to both of you. You are right,
> > inla.posterior.sample is everything that I need. Sorry for my lack
> > of knowledge
> >

> > ha scritto:
> > > Like Haavard asked, are you sure you actually need it, or are you
> > > really looking for things like "the marginal variance at each
> > > location
> > > of interest"?
> > >
> > > The information needed to compute these quantities is available,
> > > but
> > > in a way that's more amenable to the internal methods that know
> > > how to
> > > make use of them; the conditional posterior precision matrix for
> > > the
> > > joint latent field conditionally on each hyperparameter
> > > integration
> > > point is available, for example (via $misc$config).
> > >
> > > From inlabru, what we tend to do is to call generate() or
> > > predict(),
> > > that internally call inla.posterior.sample() that knows how to use
> > > the
> > > information. By specifying an evaluation expression (like the
> > > formula
> > > to bru()) you can get posterior samples from any linear or
> > > nonlinear
> > > expression involving the model components, and predict() produces
> > > summaries of that (like posterior means and standard deviations).
> > >

messages.subject: Multiple meshes in the same object
messages.subject_clean: Multiple meshes in the same object
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to test the effect of different meshes in my model, and I am creating a script where I first create the various meshes and save it to an object where then I can use them later.

I'm using foreach to speed up the process, which saves all the meshes in a list. And although every element of the list is a mesh containing all the elements of a mesh, I'm not able to access each mesh individually (i.e. R does not recognise it as a mesh class).

So I'm wondering if you have any tip on how to store different meshes in the same object, or if I should store them in different objects.

Here's a snippet of my code:
Thank you!
# Function to create meshes
makeMesh <- function(max_edge) {
inla.mesh.2d(loc = locs,
boundary = iceFree,
max.edge = c(1, 2) * max_edge,
cutoff = max_edge / 5,
offset = c(max_edge, max_edge * 5),
crs = tProj_km)
}

# List of max.edge values
max.edge.list <- list(961/4, 961/5.5, 961/9, 961/12, 961/16)

# Parallelized foreach loop
mesh_list <- foreach(max_edge_value = max.edge.list, .combine = c) %dopar% {
makeMesh(max_edge_value)
}

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] fix rho for AR1 in spatio-temporal random effect
messages.subject_clean: [r-inla] fix rho for AR1 in spatio-temporal random effect
messages.body_plain:
n = 300
rho <- 0.9
x = arima.sim(n, model=list(ar=rho))
x = x/sd(x)
s <- 0.1
y = 1 + x + rnorm(n, sd = s)
r = inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model="ar1"),
    data = data.frame(y, idx=1:n),
    family = "gaussian",
    control.family = list(
        hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/s^2), fixed = TRUE))))
summary(r)

## fix the correlation to 'rho', this needs to be converted to the
internal paramerization
inla.models()$latent$ar1$hyper$theta2$to.theta
rho.intern <- inla.models()$latent$ar1$hyper$theta2$to.theta(rho)
rr = inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model="ar1",
                    hyper = list(rho = list(initial = rho.intern,
                                            fixed = TRUE))),
    data = data.frame(y, idx=1:n),
    family = "gaussian",
    control.family = list(
        hyper = list(prec = list(initial = log(1/s^2), fixed = TRUE))))

The system's libstdc++.so.6 is linked to libstdc++.so.6.0.25. Putting both files in the /first did not change anything (same error message).

messages.body_plain:
To some degree, yes. I prefer to think in terms of Gaussian processes
rather than splines, but since one can use 2nd order b-spline basis
function in the fm_mesh_1d() constructions, the results are similar.

To have a model of the form u(t) * exp(v(t)), you could make a matern
model for u with fixed sigma parameter, and another matern field v(t)
to control the log-standard deviation of the field.
In order for that to be reliably estimable, you would need to have a
case where u(t) is replicated several times for a common v(t) field;
otherwise it won't be identifiable.

I haven't followed the whole thread, but assuming you're modelling a
time series, in pseudo-code:

matern_var_1 <- inla.spde.pcmatern(time_mesh, ..., prior.sigma = c(1, NA))
matern <- inla.spde.pcmatern(time_mesh, ...)

components = ~ u(time, model=matern_var_1, replicate =
the_replicate_index) + v(time, model=matern)
formula = observation ~ u * exp(v)

Finn

messages.subject_clean: CAR model for spatio-temporal data
messages.body_plain:
Dear INLA group,

I meet a question when I learn using INLA to fit a CAR model in space-time setting.

The following code is copied from the INLA book "Spatial and Spatio-temporal
Bayesian Models with R-INLA"

formula.par<- y ~ 1 + f(county,  model=" besag", graph=Ohio.adj,
constr=TRUE),
+ f(county1, year, model="iid", constr=TRUE),
+ year

The data contains both space (i=88) and time (t=21) dimnsions, that is to say, we have 88*21 observations.

This piece of code "f(county,  model=" besag", graph=Ohio.adj, constr=TRUE)" is used to hand spatial effects. The index is based on the "country", that is 1...88. However, we have 88*21 observations.

How did you extend this term for 1...1848 observations? Where did you put the  kronecker product? Or you extend this term through the group argument internally?

Thanks for your help
Charles LING

Hi,
That model is essentially a “functionally separable” model with county being purely spatial and county1 being a separate linear trend for each county.

For a joint space-time “covariance separable” model, you could add year as a group effect to the county component, like you mentioned.

messages.body_plain:
Complementing, I suggest you this

  formula.st <http://formula.st> <- y ~ 1 + f(county,  model=" besagproper", graph=Ohio.adj,
       group = time, control.group = list(model = "ar1"))

This defines a "functionally non-separable" model with "separable
covariance/precision", where the covariance/precision over the space
is CAR and over time is AR1.
The precision for the effect u_{1,1}, ..., u_{n,1}, u_{1,2}, ...,
u_{n,T} can be written as Qt (x) Qs, where
Qt is a precision structure, see inla.doc("ar1"), with marginal
variance equals 1 and Qs is the CAR precision, see
inla.doc("besagproper"). More details on this "group" way of doing it
is in https://github.com/hrue/r-inla/blob/devel/internal-doc/group/group-models.pdf

Elias

messages.subject: INLA crashing with bigger Dataset (250 K)
messages.subject_clean: INLA crashing with bigger Dataset (250 K)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

As part of my role, I maintain a shiny app that runs the INLA package to utilise its capabilities in setting prior information when running a model.

The package works fine until I get to a certain number of rows then it crashes. From reading around the forum, I believe this might be a memory issue – I have run this on a Windows laptop with 8GB & one with 16GB of RAM and get the same error.

Below I have a reproducible example that illustrates my issue – I have set parameters to default values for simplicity. Using 25,000 rows of data the package works fine. When I up this to 250,000 rows it crashes without any apparent reasoning. I have attached the verbose outputs.

It would be great to know if there is anything obvious I am missing or whether this is just a memory issue with INLA?

Thanks for your help in advance – it is much appreciated.
# data set example 25000 rows

small_data <- data.frame(
  y = abs(rnorm(25000)),
  x = abs(rnorm(25000))
)

str(small_data)

#> 'data.frame':    25000 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ y: num  0.026 0.303 0.204 1.482 1.725 ...
#>  $ x: num  1.4726 0.2482 0.5131 0.0507 1.3306 ...

# Linear Model Works fine

lm(formula = y ~ x, data = small_data)

#> Call:
#> lm(formula = y ~ x, data = small_data)
#>
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x
#>    0.800855    -0.009096

# INLA works fine

INLA::inla(formula = y ~ x, data = small_data, verbose = TRUE)

#> Call:
#>    "INLA::inla(formula = y ~ x, data = small_data, verbose = TRUE)"
#> Time used:
#>   Pre = 0.844, Running = 7.09, Post = 0.115, Total = 8.05

# data set example 250000 rows
big_data <- data.frame(
  y = abs(rnorm(250000)),
  x = abs(rnorm(250000))
)

str(big_data)

#> 'data.frame':    250000 obs. of  2 variables:
#>  $ y: num  0.971 0.476 0.819 0.115 1.043 ...
#>  $ x: num  0.562 0.582 0.354 2.353 0.838 ...

# Linear Model Works fine

lm(formula = y ~ x, data = big_data)
#>
#> Call:
#> lm(formula = y ~ x, data = big_data)
#>
#> Coefficients:
#> (Intercept)            x
#>    0.797617     0.002334

# INLA doesn't work

INLA::inla(formula = y ~ x, data = big_data, verbose = TRUE)

#> Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed(): The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
#>   If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Dear INLA group,

I meet a question when I  use INLA to fit a geostatistics model in space setting.

The code is as follows,

stk.e <- inla.stack(
  tag = "est",
  data = list(y = Sample_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord_withY$solid_number, numtrials = Sample_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord_withY$sample_number),
  A = list(1, A_SAM),
  effects = list(data.frame(b0 = 1, X1=Sample_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord_withY$V1, X2=Sample_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord_withY$V2, X3=Sample_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord_withY$V3), s = w.index)
)

stk.p <- inla.stack(
  tag = "pred",
  data = list(y = NA, numtrials = NA),
  A = list(1, A_TOT),
  effects = list(data.frame(b0 = 1, X1=Total_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord$V1, X2=Total_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord$V2, X3=Total_fixed_effects_country_2012_withcoord$V3), s = p.index)
)

stk.full <- inla.stack(stk.e, stk.p)

formula <- y ~ 0 + X1 + X2 + X3 + f(p, model = spde.tsp)

resp <- inla(formula,
              family = "binomial", Ntrials = numtrials,
              control.family = list(link = "logit"),
              data = inla.stack.data(stk.full),
              control.predictor = list(
                compute = TRUE, link = 1,
                A = inla.stack.A(stk.full)),
              control.compute=list(cpo = TRUE, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, config = TRUE),
              verbose = TRUE)

messages.subject: Question about Computing Cluster Efficiency
messages.subject_clean: Question about Computing Cluster Efficiency
messages.body_plain:
Hello all,

I am running a large model on a high performance computing cluster. I have the model running and am now trying to dial in the correct memory/CPU usage for submitting jobs. The model itself has many components: a zero-inflated poisson with mutliple integrated datasets sharing a joint likelihood, also including SPDE components which dramatically increases the run time. (I can provide more information if relevant).

Following successful runs with the verbose option on, I received the following information about CPU efficiency.

Stage1: Accumulated CPU-time is equivalent to 9.27 threads running at 100%
Efficiency using 32 threads = 28.96%
Stage2: Accumulated CPU-time is equivalent to 0.82 threads running at 100%
Efficiency using 32 threads = 2.56%
Total: Accumulated CPU-time is equivalent to 9.27 threads running at 100%
Efficiency using 32 threads = 28.96%

It appears that I am under utilizing the machine's resources leading to inefficient run times. Given this information, should I increase the number of CPUs and decrease the amount of memory per core (to have more processes running simultaneously) OR decrease the number of CPUs and (running closer to the 9.27 threads at 100%).

Thanks for any help!
-Matt

messages.body_plain:
You can read about parallel performance and setup in

@Article{art702,
  author =       {L. {Gaedke-Merzh\"auser} and J. {van Niekerk} and O.
                  Schenk and H. Rue},
  title =        {Parallelized integrated nested Laplace
                  approximations for fast Bayesian inference},
  journal =      {Statistics and Computing},
  year =         2022,
  keywords =     {year2022,my.own,my.cv <http://my.cv>},
  publisher =    {Springer Science and Business Media {LLC}},
  volume =       33,
  number =       1,
  doi =          {10.1007/s11222-022-10192-1}
}

there two 'types', one is parallelize function evaluations, and the
other one is to parallelize each function evaluation.

for the first, then with nh=#hyperpar, then num.threads=nh+1 or 2*nh are
good. for the second one, you need for the time being to enable the
PARDISO library.

I'll add the PARDISO library version 8 soon as the license for version 7
is running out soon, and you need to get a license at their website, or,
for a cluster, pay for one. The license issue for PARDISO has been
somewhat 'irregular' the two last years, and we're working to integrate
a free and open-source solution for sparse matrix factorization and
partial inverse. this is a lot of work, and it seems like we'll get
there during spring next year.

Make sure you're using R-4.3 and a recent version of R-INLA (testing,
preferably)

If there is anything, let me know

H

I am running the latest testing version (23.11.26) on R4.3.

messages.subject: Explained variance of fixed effects really small when including spatial autocorrelation term
messages.subject_clean: Explained variance of fixed effects really small when including spatial autocorrelation term
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I run models on a big vegetation survey dataset and control for spatial autocorrelation. I am interested in the explained variance of the fixed effects and found out that they seem to explain only a really small part of the total variance while the spatial autocorrelation term explained nearly everything. Is this possible, or is there an obvious problem in my model/calculation of variance?

Comments are highly appreciated!

Ramona

Model:
formula <- y ~ -1+ Intercept + sc_mean + sc_tas + sc_pr +
  f(spatial.field2, model = spde.pc)+
  f(inla.group(year_sampling,n=22),model = "rw2")

Mod_total_samp <- inla(formula,
                       data = inla.stack.data(StackEst1_total, spde=spde.pc),
                       family = "gaussian",
                       control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE,dic = TRUE,
                                              waic=TRUE,return.marginals.predictor=TRUE),
                       control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(StackEst1_total),
                                                compute = T,link=1))
summary(Mod_total_samp)

Calculate total explained variance:
length(observed)
length(linear_predictor)
pred<-linear_predictor[1:3105] #3105 is length of APredictor and observed
rsquared <- 1 - sum((observed - pred)^2) / sum((observed - mean(observed))^2)
rsquared:  0.8903732

Model with random effects only:
formula_total_random<- y ~ -1+
  f(spatial.field2, model = spde.pc)+
  f(inla.group(year_sampling,n=22),model = "rw2")

Mod_total_samp_random <- inla(formula_total_random,
                            data = inla.stack.data(StackEst1_total, spde=spde.pc),
                            family = "gaussian",
                            control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE,dic = TRUE,
                                                   waic=TRUE,return.marginals.predictor=TRUE),
                            control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(StackEst1_total),
                                                     compute = T,link=1))

linear_predictor_random <- Mod_total_samp_random$summary.linear.predictor$mean
pred_random<-linear_predictor_random[1:3105]
rsquared_random <- 1 - sum((observed - pred_random)^2) / sum((observed - mean(observed))^2)
rsquared_random: 0.8849892

messages.subject: cloglog problems for binary data
messages.subject_clean: cloglog problems for binary data
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

We've run into some issues with using a cloglog model for binary data (reproducibile in a simple glm).   In particular, we're getting a message of (e.g.) "GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=789" for each observation (and seemingly for each/many iterations).  The problem is not produced when using a logit link or when using the glm() function from base R.

The model does contain an offset, which has large values, but reducing/removing this doesn't seem to have any effect.

I don't know how to fix this problem.  I reckon (uneducated guesses really) that

1) It is a user error
2) There is numerical overflow issues (so that predictions are very slightly above (below) 1 (0))
3) The starting values are very far from the max
4) some combination of 3 and 4.

I have put code and simulated data in a dropbox folder.  Let me know if you can't access it. https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/00e4dko767yn42gnv1zoz/cloglogIssue1.R?rlkey=lr5gbo3488b7kyqt6z662yw2z&dl=0.  Script is pasted below (but data still on dropbox).

Any help is appreciated. Thanks,

Scott

library( INLA)

#data available from https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/tihsg9da53c6ar5z50vet/datPA.RDS?rlkey=im06zt0jnlssz1izpexsne346&dl=0

datPA <- readRDS( "~/play/cloglogIssues/datPA.RDS")

############
#Fit some models using glm()
fmGLM <- list()
#Fit the model that simulated the data. Note offset and pretty small intercept (negative on link scale)
#The fit 'works', up to some possible quasi-separation issues (haven't investigated)
fmGLM$cloglog <- glm( PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset=log(transectArea), data=datPA, family=binomial(link="cloglog"))
#estimates are quite similar to those used to simulate (1.25 and -0.85)
summary( fmGLM$cloglog)
fmGLM$logit <- glm( PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset=log(transectArea), data=datPA, family=binomial(link="logit"))
#estimates are more dissimilar, but that is probably because there is a different link.
summary( fmGLM$logit)

###########
#Now let's try the same with inla()
fmINLA <- list()
fmINLA$cloglog <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic")
#this seems to have more-or-less failed with lots of errors like:
#...
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=990
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=991
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=992
#GMRFLib_2order_approx: rescue NAN/INF values in logl for idx=993
#...
#In fact, there appears to be an error for each datum, possibly for each iteration of the optimisation
#Perhaps not surprisingly, the estimates are... not similar.  Probably stuck at starting values?
summary( fmINLA$cloglog)

#will logit be any different?
fmINLA$logit <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                       family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="logit"), inla.mode="classic")
#no warning/error messages
#and the estimates appear to be very similar to those from the logit GLM.
summary( fmINLA$logit)

#########
#FWIW, add strong priors to effects may 'help' with the possible quasi-separation.
fmINLA$cloglog_prior1 <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean=0, prec=1/0.1))
#same errors and similar summary

#what about when the intercept prior is shifted to be negative -- may affect starting values?
fmINLA$cloglog_prior2 <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, prec.intercept=1))

##########
#FWIW, reducing scale of offset or removing completely doesn't seem to solve the problem either
#is it a problem with the size of the offset?
#no, but there are fewer NAN/INF warnings
fmINLA$smallerOffset <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = log( datPA$transectArea/1000000), data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, prec.intercept=1))

fmINLA$noOffset <- inla(PA ~ 1+SoilMoisture+bio_4, offset = 0, data=datPA, Ntrials=1,
                 family = "binomial", control.family=list(link="cloglog"), inla.mode="classic",
 control.fixed=list(mean.intercept=-15, prec.intercept=1))
